sources.title: App Review Guidelines
sources.summary: UGC and social apps need objectionable-content filtering, reporting with timely response, abusive-user blocking, and published contact information; creator content above the rating needs age controls.
sources.applicability: Apps with posts, comments, chat, profiles, shared media, communities, creator content, or other UGC.

sources.title: App Review Guidelines
sources.summary: Submit a final and stable app with complete metadata, functional URLs and backends, review access, and reviewable in-app purchases; scrub placeholders and obvious technical problems.
sources.applicability: All submissions.

sources.title: App Review Guidelines
sources.summary: Metadata, screenshots, previews, privacy information, price claims, age answers, and review notes must accurately reflect current functionality and purchases.
sources.applicability: All submissions and localizations.

sources.title: App Review Guidelines
sources.summary: Digital features and content generally require In-App Purchase; the guideline says developers should provide a restore mechanism for restorable purchases, and purchase representations must not mislead.
sources.applicability: Apps selling or unlocking digital content, features, credits, or services.

sources.title: App Review Guidelines
sources.summary: Auto-renewable subscriptions must provide ongoing value; section 3.1.2(c) says developers should clearly describe what the customer receives for the price before subscription.
sources.applicability: Apps offering auto-renewable subscriptions.

sources.title: App Review Guidelines
sources.summary: Apps need adequate standalone utility or lasting entertainment and should be more than a repackaged website, advertisement, link collection, or lightly customized template.
sources.applicability: All apps, especially wrappers, catalogs, templates, and low-feature utilities.

sources.title: App Review Guidelines
sources.summary: Apps using third-party or social login for the primary account must also offer an equivalent privacy-preserving login service unless a listed exception applies.
sources.applicability: Primary-account authentication using Google, Facebook, X, LinkedIn, Amazon, WeChat, or similar services.

sources.title: App Review Guidelines
sources.summary: Apps need an accessible privacy policy, applicable consent, clear purpose strings, respect for access decisions, and in-app account deletion when account creation is supported; the guideline separately says apps should minimize data collection.
sources.applicability: All apps; individual clauses depend on collection, protected resources, and accounts.

sources.title: App Review Guidelines
sources.summary: Personal data may not be used, transmitted, or shared without permission; sharing with third parties, including third-party AI, must be disclosed and explicitly permitted.
sources.applicability: Apps transmitting or sharing personal data, including to server-hosted AI providers.

sources.title: App Review Guidelines
sources.section: 5.6 Developer Code of Conduct; Rejections and Appeals
sources.summary: Developer representations and communications must be truthful, relevant, respectful, and current; rejected developers may communicate with App Review or appeal with evidence.
sources.applicability: Rejection responses, review communications, and appeals.

sources.title: App Review
sources.summary: Apple highlights crashes, broken links, placeholders, incomplete review access, misleading behavior, privacy-policy defects, and insufficient lasting value as common issues.
sources.applicability: All pre-submission audits.

sources.title: Offering account deletion in your app
sources.section: Account deletion guidance; Frequently asked questions
sources.summary: Account deletion must be easy to find, initiate in-app, cover the account and associated data, and not be replaced by deactivation. Explain timing when deletion is delayed and subscription effects when applicable; legally required retention can remain with disclosure.
sources.applicability: Apps supporting account creation, including automatically created guest accounts.

sources.title: TN3194: Handling account deletions and revoking tokens for Sign in with Apple
sources.section: Invalidate a user session; account deletion handling
sources.summary: Sign in with Apple account deletion handling includes revoking Apple tokens and removing developer-held user data and sessions.
sources.applicability: Apps using Sign in with Apple.

sources.title: Sign in with Apple
sources.summary: Apple documents the native and web authentication capability and related server APIs.
sources.applicability: Apps implementing Sign in with Apple.

sources.title: Platform version information
sources.section: Platform version information; App Review information
sources.summary: Defines required screenshots, description, keywords, Support URL, copyright, review contact, notes, and non-expiring demo-account information.
sources.applicability: App Store Connect version metadata and review access.

sources.title: App information
sources.summary: Defines app name, subtitle, privacy URL, Bundle ID, content rights, age rating, Kids selection, and license-agreement properties.
sources.applicability: App-level App Store Connect metadata.

sources.title: Upload app previews and screenshots
sources.summary: Requires one to ten screenshots in supported formats and describes localization and device-size behavior; app previews are optional.
sources.applicability: Store listing media for each supported platform and applicable localization.

sources.title: Localize app information
sources.summary: Explains localized metadata behavior, primary-language fallback, and how screenshots and fields are inherited or localized.
sources.applicability: Apps with multiple App Store localizations.

sources.title: Set an app age rating
sources.section: Age rating questionnaire; overrides; regional ratings
sources.summary: Age rating is required; questionnaire answers must reflect content and capabilities, and Unrated apps cannot publish on the App Store.
sources.applicability: All apps.

sources.title: Manage app privacy
sources.section: App privacy responses and privacy policy information
sources.summary: App privacy answers and privacy-policy information in App Store Connect must accurately cover the app and integrated third parties.
sources.applicability: All App Store apps.

sources.title: App Privacy Details
sources.section: Data collection, tracking, data types, and privacy links
sources.summary: Defines collection, optional disclosure exceptions, tracking, linked data, data purposes, data categories, and required privacy-policy link behavior.
sources.applicability: Privacy Nutrition Label preparation and reconciliation.

sources.title: Privacy manifest files
sources.summary: PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy records collected-data practices, tracking domains, and required-reason API declarations for app and SDK bundles.
sources.applicability: Apps or SDKs using required-reason APIs, collecting data, enabling collection, tracking, or listed SDKs.

sources.title: Describing data use in privacy manifests
sources.summary: Privacy manifests use Apple-defined data types, linkage and tracking flags, and allowed purposes for app or SDK collection declarations.
sources.applicability: Apps and SDKs declaring data collection.

sources.title: Describing use of required reason API
sources.section: Overview; reporting privacy accessed API usage
sources.summary: Each applicable executable or dynamic-library bundle must declare approved, accurate reasons for covered APIs; undeclared use is not accepted by App Store Connect.
sources.applicability: Apps and third-party SDKs using covered API categories.

sources.title: Third-party SDK requirements
sources.section: Privacy manifests; signatures; SDKs requiring a manifest and signature
sources.summary: Listed SDKs and repackaged copies require privacy manifests; listed binary SDKs also require signatures in the specified submission cases.
sources.applicability: Apps including an Apple-listed third-party SDK.

sources.title: App Tracking Transparency
sources.summary: Documents the ATT framework, authorization request, status values, and NSUserTrackingUsageDescription implementation surface.
sources.applicability: Implementation in apps whose behavior meets Apple's tracking policy definition.

sources.title: User privacy and data use
sources.section: Permission to track; tracking definition and examples; exceptions
sources.summary: Defines tracking for App Store policy, lists examples and narrow exceptions, and requires ATT permission before tracking or accessing the advertising identifier.
sources.applicability: Apps linking user or device data with third-party data for targeted advertising, advertising measurement, or sharing with data brokers, subject to Apple's stated exceptions.

sources.title: Human Interface Guidelines: Privacy
sources.summary: Request access only when needed and use specific, plain purpose strings that explain how and why the app uses the protected resource.
sources.applicability: System permission prompts and privacy-related interface behavior.

sources.title: Human Interface Guidelines: Accessibility
sources.summary: Audit interfaces for perceivable, adaptable, and operable experiences, including larger text, VoiceOver, sufficient contrast, alternatives to single sensory cues, and familiar interactions.
sources.applicability: All user interfaces; exact checks depend on content and controls.

sources.title: Human Interface Guidelines: Layout
sources.summary: Interfaces should adapt to device size, orientation, safe areas, readable widths, system text sizing, and supported multitasking configurations.
sources.applicability: iPhone and iPad interfaces, including orientation and Split View where supported.

sources.title: Restoring purchased products
sources.summary: Give customers a user-initiated mechanism, such as Restore Purchases, to restore eligible purchases; do not automatically prompt for restoration at launch.
sources.applicability: Apps with restorable non-consumables or subscriptions.

sources.title: Transaction.currentEntitlements
sources.summary: StoreKit 2 exposes the latest transactions entitling a customer to non-consumables and subscriptions; refunded or revoked products are omitted.
sources.applicability: StoreKit 2 entitlement reconciliation.

sources.title: Testing In-App Purchases with sandbox
sources.section: Prepare for sandbox testing; product requests; transactions; subscriptions; refunds
sources.summary: Sandbox uses real App Store Connect product information and supports tests for product requests, purchase outcomes, interrupted and external transactions, renewals, billing failures, refunds, and server notifications without charging testers.
sources.applicability: Apps offering In-App Purchases or subscriptions.

sources.title: Testing at all stages of development with Xcode and the sandbox
sources.section: Test environments and common StoreKit scenarios
sources.summary: Use StoreKit Testing, Sandbox, and TestFlight at appropriate stages and cover purchases, restores, subscription changes, failures, and transactions that occur outside the app.
sources.applicability: StoreKit implementation and release verification.

sources.title: Human Interface Guidelines: In-app purchase
sources.section: Making signup effortless; subscription signup information
sources.summary: Subscription signup should show name, duration, provided value, correctly localized billing amount, restore/sign-in access, and clear free-trial conversion; legal links are also expected.
sources.applicability: Paywalls and purchase interfaces.

sources.title: Auto-renewable Subscriptions
sources.summary: Subscription signup must include name, duration, service, prominent full renewal price, restore/sign-in path, and trial duration and post-trial price; metadata needs Terms and Privacy links.
sources.applicability: Auto-renewable subscription apps.

sources.title: In-App Purchase information
sources.section: General information; localizable information; App Review Screenshot
sources.summary: Defines IAP identifiers, localized display fields, review notes, and review screenshot requirements and limits.
sources.applicability: In-App Purchase records in App Store Connect.

sources.title: Offer auto-renewable subscriptions
sources.section: Create products; add localizations; review information
sources.summary: Configure a subscription group, products, duration, price, availability, review information, and localized metadata in App Store Connect.
sources.applicability: Auto-renewable subscriptions in App Store Connect.

sources.title: Overview of export compliance
sources.summary: Apps using or incorporating encryption must complete the App Store Connect determination and provide documentation when required; Info.plist can record exempt/no-documentation outcomes.
sources.applicability: Apps using or incorporating encryption.

sources.title: Overview of submitting for review
sources.summary: Explains how app versions and related content enter App Review, how review messages are organized, and which items may be submitted together or separately.
sources.applicability: Submission preparation and App Review communication.

sources.title: Human Interface Guidelines: Generative AI
sources.summary: For server models, minimize sharing, disclose off-device transfer and storage or training, ask before using personal or usage data, and provide opt-out where applicable.
sources.applicability: Apps with generative-AI features.

sources.title: Upcoming Requirements
sources.section: SDK minimum requirements; approved reasons for APIs; age rating updates
sources.summary: As of April 28, 2026, iOS/iPadOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS uploads require Xcode 26 and the corresponding platform 26 SDK; the page also tracks required-reason APIs and age-rating submission gates.
sources.applicability: Covered iOS/iPadOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS App Store Connect uploads; this entry does not assert a macOS 26 SDK gate.

sources.title: Age rating questionnaire now includes social media questions
sources.summary: Social-media capability questions are available now and become required for new apps and updates beginning in September 2026.
sources.applicability: Apps that redistribute, amplify, or enable interaction with UGC through feeds or discovery.
